overall_summary: Bitcoin is under clear pressure with ETF outflows, miner selling, and a confirmed break below the 200-week average. A strong dollar, sticky import prices, and hawkish Fed backdrop reinforce the risk-off tone. Escalating US-Iran strikes and broader geopolitical stress add further downside catalysts for crypto.
key_points: ETF outflows and miner selling hit Bitcoin
Strong dollar and hawkish Fed weigh heavily
Abu Dhabi steady IBIT holdings offer limited support

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $240M as CryptoQuant Flags Bearish Phase
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly 240 million dollars in net outflows on November 17, with BlackRock's IBIT alone accounting for about 209 million. That reversed a one-day inflow that had briefly ended a multi-session outflow streak. CryptoQuant said Bitcoin has returned to a bearish market phase with demand contracting at its fastest pace in months and sentiment at multi-month lows. Traders should care because ETF flows have been a primary driver of spot demand, and continued redemptions remove a key bid while price sits near recent lows around 64,000.
items.impact: Sustains institutional selling pressure and weakens near-term demand

items.title: Bitcoin Lags Nvidia Beat as Basis Trade Dries Up
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 1 percent toward 64,100 dollars even as Nasdaq futures rose after Nvidia crushed earnings and raised guidance. Crypto's basis trade, the carry from holding spot against short perps, has collapsed to just 3 to 5 percent annualized, near or below Treasury yields, so capital is rotating out. Fed October minutes arrive later today with markets pricing a 96 percent chance of a December rate hike. This matters for traders because crypto is failing to catch the risk rebound and face both micro liquidity drought and macro headwinds.
items.impact: Keeps price capped ahead of key macro event with thin derivatives support

items.title: MARA Sells More Bitcoin, 2026 Total Tops $3 Billion
items.summary: Miner MARA transferred another 366 BTC worth roughly 23 million dollars, pushing its tracked 2026 sales to about 40,581 BTC or 3.03 billion dollars. After its Q3 report it sold another 1,714 BTC in eight days to repay loans and fund an AI infrastructure pivot, leaving roughly 20,000 BTC that analysts expect will keep hitting the market. Capriole noted some of the strongest institutional selling on record. Traders should watch this because large miner supply arrives into already thin ETF demand and extreme fear conditions.
items.impact: Adds persistent spot supply from a major corporate holder

items.title: Bitcoin Breaks Below 200-Week Average on 12% Slide
items.summary: Bitcoin's recent drop took it through the 200-week moving average with a roughly 12 percent move, an event seen only three times since 2013. In each prior case price stood higher three months later, though often after further 10 to 17 percent downside first. Wintermute has flagged risk of a slide into the 50,000s amid rate-hike bets, while Glassnode notes the largest bids at 60,000 and below since August. This is critical because it tests a major long-term technical level whose resolution will set the medium-term tone.
items.impact: Unresolved key support test with historical rebound odds but near-term downside risk

items.title: Bitcoin Outpaces Gold as Both Tumble on Rate Bets
items.summary: Bitcoin held near 64,000 dollars while gold fell about 2 percent, lifting the bitcoin-to-gold ratio above its 200-day moving average and extending a series of higher lows since March. One bitcoin now buys roughly 17 ounces of gold, up more than 40 percent from the March low. Both assets face pressure from a firm dollar and nearly 97 percent odds of a December Fed hike ahead of today's minutes. Relative strength versus the classic safe haven is a constructive longer-term signal even while absolute prices remain under macro stress.
items.impact: Signals relative resilience but does not reverse absolute selling pressure

items.title: Abu Dhabi Funds Hold Steady With Over $1B in IBIT
items.summary: Q3 13F filings show Abu Dhabi's Mubadala and Abu Dhabi Investment Council maintained combined holdings of over 1 billion dollars in BlackRock's IBIT, with share counts unchanged from the prior quarter. The Investment Council now has IBIT as more than half its reported US portfolio. Other large players including Susquehanna and Brevan Howard increased stakes in the same period. This demonstrates sovereign and institutional conviction holding through the drawdown and offers a counterpoint to recent ETF outflow data.
items.impact: Reinforces long-term institutional and sovereign demand narrative

items.title: FOMC Minutes Due Today After Hawkish Fed Speeches
items.summary: Markets are laser-focused on the Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes releasing at 2 p.m. Eastern today. The Fed held rates at 3.75 to 4 percent last month with two dissenters wanting a hike. New York Fed's John Williams said more tightening is likely needed but no dramatic action, while St. Louis Fed's Alberto Musalem called for several hikes by spring 2027. Traders should care because this sets the tone for December's nearly certain 25 basis point hike and the path beyond, driving dollar strength and higher yields that pressure risk assets including crypto.
items.impact: Reinforces higher-for-longer rates, stronger USD, softer risk appetite

items.title: US Dollar Holds Near 19-Month High on Hike Bets
items.summary: The dollar index sits near 103.6 to 103.8, its strongest level since April 2025, after retail sales, hot import prices, and hawkish Fed comments. Ten-year Treasury yields hover around 5.08 to 5.10 percent. Markets price roughly 96 percent odds of a 25 basis point December hike. Crypto traders should watch this closely because a firm dollar and elevated yields typically weigh on Bitcoin and other risk assets by raising opportunity costs and tightening financial conditions.
items.impact: Supports USD strength and higher yields, headwind for BTC and equities

items.title: October Retail Sales Rise 0.2 Percent In Line
items.summary: US retail sales increased 0.2 percent month-over-month in October, matching forecasts and slowing from 0.8 percent prior. Control group sales excluding autos and gas were firmer at around 0.6 percent. Auto sales dragged while online and other categories held up. This keeps consumer demand resilient enough to support the case for further Fed tightening even as real volumes were softer after inflation. Traders care because solid spending reduces recession odds but sustains rate-hike pressure that can cap crypto rallies.
items.impact: Supports growth narrative but cements December hike pricing

items.title: Housing Starts Fall to 1.246 Million in October
items.summary: Housing starts dropped 4.6 percent to a 1.246 million annualized rate in October after September was revised higher to 1.306 million. Single-family starts rebounded but multifamily plunged. Building permits edged lower to 1.412 million. The print came in softer than some expectations and marks one of the weakest levels since 2020. Higher mortgage rates continue to squeeze residential activity. This matters for markets as it shows rate-sensitive sectors cracking while the broader economy stays resilient enough for the Fed to stay hawkish.
items.impact: Highlights rate pain in housing without derailing hike bets

items.title: Import Prices Jump 1.1 Percent, Beat Expectations
items.summary: US import prices rose 1.1 percent in October, well above the 0.7 percent forecast, matching the prior month's gain. Fuel prices climbed 3.6 percent and nonfuel prices accelerated, with capital goods posting a record monthly jump. Export prices also rose 1.1 percent. This adds to evidence that inflation pressures remain broad. For traders it reinforces the Fed's need to tighten further, supporting the dollar and yields while pressuring gold and risk assets like Bitcoin in the near term.
items.impact: Hot pipeline inflation strengthens case for more Fed hikes

items.title: Industrial Production Drops 0.4 Percent in October
items.summary: US industrial production fell 0.4 percent in October after a 0.7 percent gain, missing expectations for a small rise. Utilities plunged 4.3 percent and mining declined while manufacturing rose 0.3 percent on a rebound in motor vehicles and AI-related equipment. Capacity utilization slipped to 76.4 percent. The mixed picture shows factory resilience amid softer overall output. Crypto and equity traders should note it does little to ease rate-hike expectations given still-firm demand and inflation data elsewhere.
items.impact: Soft headline but manufacturing holds; limited shift to Fed path

items.title: US Strikes Iran Qeshm Missile Site; Iran Hits Kuwait, Bahrain
items.summary: US jets hit an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz in self-defense after Iranian drones targeted Bahrain. Iran then widened attacks, striking a US base in Kuwait and again hitting Bahrain, with defenses intercepting drones and missiles. A third US carrier is in the region amid the ongoing war. Traders should watch this closely because Hormuz disruptions keep oil risk premiums elevated and can spark broader risk-off moves across equities and crypto.
items.impact: Elevates oil prices and risk-off pressure on Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Trump Arrives in China for Historic Xi-Putin Trilateral
items.summary: President Trump landed in Shenzhen where Xi Jinping greeted him with a rare hug ahead of APEC. Xi and Putin already met, and the three leaders hold unprecedented trilateral talks Thursday covering Ukraine, Iran, nuclear arms, trade and AI. Smaller nations fear a new spheres-of-influence deal. This is the biggest diplomatic event in years and any de-escalation signals or breakthroughs could sharply reverse risk sentiment for crypto traders.
items.impact: Outcome unresolved; potential catalyst for risk-on or further volatility

items.title: Ukraine Collapses Key Section of Crimean Kerch Bridge
items.summary: Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed a major road arch and span of the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea in a multi-stage operation. Zelensky called it unprecedented after weeks of degrading air defenses. Russia vows to rebuild and struck Kyiv bridges in response. The hit humiliates Putin just before his summit with Trump and Xi and complicates Russian logistics, keeping the Ukraine war hot and risk assets on edge.
items.impact: Prolongs Ukraine conflict uncertainty and supports safe-haven flows

items.title: Oil Steadies Near $93 Amid Fresh Hormuz Clashes and Surplus Fears
items.summary: Brent hovered around ninety-three dollars as US-Iran strikes and tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz added supply risks, offset by recovering Gulf exports and IEA surplus forecasts. Freight rates hit highs while flows continue under escort. Energy shocks feed inflation and Fed hawkishness, which crypto traders know can pressure risk assets even if crude does not spike dramatically.
items.impact: Mixed oil signal limits extreme moves but sustains volatility premium

items.title: UK and Australia Sanction Israeli Settlement Builders
items.summary: Britain blacklisted eight Israeli construction firms building West Bank settlements and a group blocking Gaza aid, aiming to protect a two-state solution ahead of E1 tenders. Australia followed with sanctions on individuals and organizations linked to settlement expansion and violence. Israel vowed retaliation. These moves signal Western policy shifts that could affect regional stability and broader Middle East risk pricing.
items.impact: Adds diplomatic friction but limited immediate market catalyst

items.title: Third US Carrier Arrives as Iran Dirty Bomb Threats Surface
items.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt joined two other carriers in the Middle East, boosting US firepower amid the Iran stalemate. Trump said the US is looking into reports Iran may plot dirty bomb or chemical attacks on officials or Washington. Gulf shipping and bases remain targets. Heightened military posture raises the chance of miscalculation that would hit energy markets and risk appetite hard.
items.impact: Increases escalation probability and safe-haven demand
